58	CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
59	-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
60	--
61	--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
62	--                     never read again; its replacement is.
63	--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
64	--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
65	--
66	-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
67	--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
68	--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
69	--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
70	--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
71	--   4 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it.
72	--   5 BLOCKED            no reading covers the pair AND the source carries a
73	--                        processing_blocked_reason that says its text could not be obtained
74	--                        or read: nothing of it can be read, so the pair is not reading
75	--                        debt until the block clears.
76	--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
77	-- A recorded reading ALWAYS outranks a block: a reading of held bytes proves the block
78	-- lifted (migration 122 ranked BLOCKED above the readings and masked them). A reading
79	-- COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id (the
80	-- parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1 and
81	-- 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading recorded;
82	-- 3 wins over 4 because a full reading supersedes a partial one of the same source.
83	--
84	-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read": the
85	-- writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. It admits exactly the
86	-- processing_blocked_reason values whose CHECK comment (migration 091) names an obstacle to
87	-- the text: no-full-text, paywalled, no-doi, not-indexed, language. `no-quantified-claims`
88	-- and `superseded` are copies of typed facts (a recorded reading; superseded_by_ref_id) and
89	-- the writers refuse them by pointer. `out-of-scope` and `tier-not-required` say no text
90	-- was unobtainable, so they are treated as NULL (the source owes its reading) pending
91	-- owner question 8 of the round-2 adjudication.
92	--
93	-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
94	-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
95	-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
96	WITH pairs AS (
97	    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
98	      FROM evidence_sources e
99	     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
100	     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
101	       AND p.status = 'active'
102	),
103	best AS (
104	    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
105	           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
106	             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
107	               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
108	                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
109	             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
110	                      s.scan_id DESC
111	             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
112	      FROM pairs pr
113	)
114	SELECT b.ref_id,
115	       b.parameter_id,
116	       CASE
117	         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
118	                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
119	                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
120	         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
121	                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
122	                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
123	         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
124	         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'

126	              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'no-doi', 'not-indexed', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
127	         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
128	       END AS status,

130	       s.text_scope,

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Derive the WHOLE text of a source's held PDF or web page, registered under its ref_id.
3	
4	WHY THIS EXISTS (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.3 step 1; tooling T1, owner approval D8,
5	2026-10-09). The scan contract reads every admitted source against the whole parameter
6	list, and a reading can only be as complete as the text it reads. Batch 23 extracted text
7	by hand from PDFs it held whole -- REF-01027's derived text covers 4 of its 79 pages -- and
8	nothing could say how much of a document a reading had actually seen. A reading recorded
9	as `full` over four pages would make the catalogue imply "no code sets a requirement"
10	where nobody read the code (the GAP-061 shape). This derives ALL pages, in the page-marker
11	form the batch 23 texts already use (`[PDF page N of M]`), so `db.py record-scan` can
12	COMPUTE pages read against pages held instead of being told.
13	
14	IT IS NOT A SECOND COPY OF THE LOG'S MECHANISMS. Which files belong to a source is
15	`retrieval_log.artefacts_for_source`; the manifest line is `retrieval_log.record_file`
16	(kind `text-extraction`, the kind batch 23 used); decoding a web page is
17	`retrieval_log.decode_artefact`. The derived text carries the source's ref_id, so quotes
18	read from it verify SCOPED (`retrieval_log.locate_quote`) -- which is what lets
19	`observe-term` refuse a quote found only in some other source's bytes.
20	
21	NO NETWORK. It reads bytes already persisted under retrieval-log/. A source with no held
22	PDF or HTML has nothing to derive from, and the reading is recorded as partial, fragment
23	or abstract (or the document is retrieved first, R10).
24	
25	    python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id REF-01027 --session <session>
26	    python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id REF-01027 --session <session> \\
27	        --artefact 1bc0a3fe0bdf78f2.pdf        # when the source holds several files
28	
29	`--session` names the retrieval-log directory the derived text is written into: the
30	session doing the reading, not the one that fetched the PDF (the manifest line names the
31	PDF it was derived from). Prints pages read / pages total, the pages with no text layer
32	(render those with page_image.py and read them), the sha256, and the record-scan call.
33	
34	Exit 0 written or already registered; 1 nothing derivable; 2 refused or ambiguous.
35	"""
36	import argparse
37	import hashlib
38	import html
39	import re
40	import sys
41	from pathlib import Path
42	
43	HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
44	sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
45	sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE.parent))
46	import retrieval_log                                                  # noqa: E402
47	import dbcore                                                         # noqa: E402
48	
49	_DERIVABLE = (".pdf", ".html")
50	_SCRIPT_STYLE = re.compile(r"<(script|style|noscript)\b[^>]*>.*?</\1\s*>", re.I | re.S)
51	_BLOCK = re.compile(r"<\s*(br|/p|/div|/li|/tr|/h[1-6]|/td|/th|/section|/article)\b[^>]*>",
52	                    re.I)
53	_TAGS = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")
54	
55	
56	def pdf_text(path):
57	    """(text, pages_total, empty_pages) -- every page, each headed by its marker.
58	
59	    The join reproduces the batch 23 files byte-for-byte in shape: the marker line, the
60	    page's text as PyMuPDF returns it, and one blank line before the next marker.
61	    """
62	    import pymupdf
63	    with pymupdf.open(str(path)) as doc:
64	        n = doc.page_count
65	        parts, empty = [], []
66	        for i, page in enumerate(doc, start=1):
67	            t = page.get_text()
68	            if not retrieval_log.normalise_quote(t):
69	                empty.append(i)
70	            parts.append(f"[PDF page {i} of {n}]\n{t}")
71	    return "\n".join(parts), n, empty
72	
73	
74	def html_text(path, content_type=None):
75	    """Visible text of a saved web page (scripts and styles dropped, tags stripped)."""
76	    body, enc = retrieval_log.decode_artefact(Path(path).read_bytes(), content_type)
77	    if body is None:
78	        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: bytes not decodable ({enc})")
79	    body = _SCRIPT_STYLE.sub(" ", body)
80	    body = _BLOCK.sub("\n", body)
81	    body = html.unescape(_TAGS.sub(" ", body))
82	    lines = [re.sub(r"[ \t ]+", " ", ln).strip() for ln in body.splitlines()]
83	    return "\n".join(ln for ln in lines if ln) + "\n"
84	
85	
86	def main():
87	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
88	                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
89	    ap.add_argument("--ref-id", required=True)
90	    ap.add_argument("--session", required=True,
91	                    help="the reading session; the derived text is written into its log")
92	    ap.add_argument("--artefact", help="which held PDF/HTML to derive from, by file name")
93	    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",

97

99	        row = conn.execute("SELECT url, superseded_by_ref_id FROM evidence_sources "
100	                           "WHERE ref_id = ?", (ref,)).fetchone()
101	    if row is None:
102	        print(f"REFUSING: {ref} is not an admitted source.", file=sys.stderr)
103	        return 2
104	    if row["superseded_by_ref_id"]:
105	        print(f"REFUSING: {ref} is superseded by {row['superseded_by_ref_id']} -- a "
106	              f"tombstone is never read again; derive the replacement's text instead.",
107	              file=sys.stderr)
108	        return 2
109	
110	    held = retrieval_log.artefacts_for_source(ref, row["url"])
111	    cands = [h for h in held if not h["derived"] and h["exists"]
112	             and h["path"].suffix.lower() in _DERIVABLE]
113	    if args.artefact:
114	        pick = [h for h in cands if h["artefact"] == args.artefact]
115	        if not pick:
116	            print(f"REFUSING: --artefact {args.artefact!r} is not a PDF or HTML file saved "
117	                  f"for {ref}. Saved for it: "
118	                  f"{[h['artefact'] for h in held] or 'nothing'}", file=sys.stderr)
119	            return 2
120	        src = pick[0]
121	    else:
122	        pdfs = [h for h in cands if h["path"].suffix.lower() == ".pdf"]
123	        pages = [h for h in cands if h["path"].suffix.lower() == ".html"]
124	        if len(pdfs) == 1:
125	            src = pdfs[0]
126	        elif not pdfs and len(pages) == 1:
127	            src = pages[0]

Count it, never quote it: `python3 -c "import sqlite3;print(sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True).execute('select count(*) from source_value_extractions').fetchone()[0])"`. The clause below is conditioned on that count being zero and stops applying the moment it is not. Genealogy is an available discriminator with nothing yet to discriminate — the extraction pass is Phase-E work. No determination may cite root-independence until rows exist, and an empty view returning no roots is not a finding of no independence: it is the Altman & Bland distinction (§9) applied to this table.]`

## 5. Determinations — states, and what each state is *about*

Each (`parameter_id` × at least one of `identity_code`, `icf_code`, `needs_code`, `medical_code`) cell holds one of four states (`evidence-methodology.md` §2; storage: migration 026): `stated`, `provisional`, `pending`, `not_applicable`. The determination is written by a pure function — same evidence + same `rule_version` ⇒ same state and same `derivation_sha` (`workplan/best-practices-assessment-system.md` §3) — and no `stated` or `provisional` determination can exist without non-empty `governing_refs` (anti-hallucination, DR-2026-07-12 item 10; `pending`/`not_applicable` rows carry a gap link or rationale instead).

**Scale-tagging** `[NEW — DR-gated: G1b]`. Every determination is tagged with the design scale its claim speaks to, and the tag governs what the determination may be *called* in every rendering:

- A determination anchored in T1/Co-1/T2/Co-2 (with T3 per its threshold DR) is a **Population-Mode best-practice determination** — the only kind rendered at anchoring strength (`●` band, subject to its conditioning). Since the weighted-strength amendment (owner directive 2026-07-21, Option A; `tier-system.md` §8) the phrase "best practice" is no longer exclusive to it: the weak band below extends the phrase, never the strength (the ◐ band applies at citation level only — footnote ††).
**8.4 Co-1/T1 divergence at Person Mode (entrance threshold, `evidence-methodology.md` §4).** Where clinical evidence and lived-experience evidence diverge on a parameter, the divergence is recorded and a synthesis approach is required and rendered (never hidden). At Person Mode the asymmetry principle governs: the person's own assessed need — not the population median, not the DPO position, not the CPG — resolves the value; the population range informs the assessment but does not bound it. The OT register presents the functional parameter and the population-range scaffold the assessment starts from; the plain-language register tells the person what is theirs to decide.

## 9. Academic rigour and ethics — the standing commitments

**Rigour.** The architecture's methodological anchors, and where each is argued in full: correspondence to GRADE/JBI/SIGN and why wholesale GRADE adoption is insufficient for built-environment claims (`references/methodology-evidence-hierarchy-mapping.md` v2 — the directness layer *is* GRADE's indirectness domain, applied bidirectionally; synthesis-above-primary follows GRADE; the co-primacy of lived experience is a declared, argued departure, not an oversight); categorical rather than numeric conditioning (no false-precision scores, `schemas/directness.py` BOUNDARY note); determinism and reproducibility (pure determination function, `rule_version` + `derivation_sha`); falsifiability (every `stated`/`provisional` cell records what evidence would overturn it, `workplan/best-practices-assessment-system.md` §3 item 6); absence-of-evidence ≠ evidence-of-absence (Altman & Bland 1995, applied to cells in §2.4 and — via G2 — to the project's own assessment metadata); and the anti-hallucination gate (no determination without resolvable `governing_refs`).

**Ethics.** The commitments are structural, not aspirational: CRPD Art. 4.3 grounds Co-1 co-primacy (Art. 9 ≈ Universal Mode floor; Art. 5 reasonable accommodation ≈ Person Mode; the full article-by-article critique is `governance/armature_v3_review.md`); epistemic justice is engineered — testimonial justice via Co-1's non-substitutable co-primacy and G3's refusal to let population-grain speech stand in for individuals, hermeneutical justice via the plain-language register receiving the *same* determination tuple as the technical one (I1: access to the same facts, not a simplified sub-truth); the carer is a distinct role, never a proxy for the disabled person (Art. 12 supported-not-substituted decision-making, `armature_v4.md` §4.5); representation-checking by disabled readers is an elevated-weight use-pattern whose failure overrides designer convenience (`audience-priority.md` §Within-primary); and the solo-authorship limit is declared on every Co-1-governed determination — pre-launch engagement with Co-1 is evidence-level, not participation-level, and CRPD Art. 4.3 is thereby honored in partial form only (`mission-and-epistemics.md` §Operational reality). Integrity here means the limits are rendered, not just recorded.

## 10. What would falsify this architecture, and how it is checked

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/scan_debt.py — which (source, parameter) pairs nobody has read in full?

WHY THIS EXISTS (tooling T1, 2026-10-09; catalogue-plan-v2 sections 3.8 and 8.2). The
owner's requirement: "Ensure that we can add and expand parameter catalogue as required
based on new information we come across." A parameter promoted in month three is owed a
look in month one's sources, and nothing showed that debt: the catalogue could imply "no
code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code for that quantity, while every gate
read green -- how GAP-061's figures were lost. `v_scan_ledger` (migration 103) derives a
status for every unsuperseded source x active parameter from the extractions and the
reading record (source_scans); this counts the pairs still owed.

DEBT = NOT-READ + READ-PARTIAL pairs. EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT and READ-NOTHING-FOUND are
accounted for. READ-PARTIAL is debt because a partial, fragment or abstract reading cannot
say a quantity is absent from the pages it did not see.

NO DEBT BASELINE, deliberately (the "no floor" this check was asked for). Debt RISES
legitimately -- every parameter promoted and every source admitted adds pairs -- so a
ratchet-down baseline would turn red on correct work. It is advisory and red whenever
debt > 0: the honest state of a catalogue that has not been read. Its readers: the next
cohort's worklist (the pairs printed below), the catalogue's evidence-state line, and the
Release 0 acceptance test (plan section 12, Q12), which will scope it to that source set.

EXAMINED is the number of ledger pairs. Zero pairs means no unsuperseded source or no
active parameter -- a corpus clear, which this project has done once (2026-09-13) -- and
the registry floor (min_items: 1) makes that visible rather than a silent pass.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/audit/scan_debt.py [--limit N]
Exit 0 no debt; 1 debt; 2 cannot run (no database, or a pre-103 schema).
"""
import argparse
import os
import sqlite3
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", REPO / "data" / "guidebook.db"))
DEBT = ("NOT-READ", "READ-PARTIAL")
# BLOCKED (migrations 122, 123): the source carries a processing_blocked_reason that the
# ledger classes as an obstacle to the text (no full text, paywalled, ...), so nothing of it
# can be read and the pair is not debt until the block clears. A reason the ledger does not
# class as an obstacle leaves the pair NOT-READ. Printed apart so it is visible, never
# silently paid down: until 2026-11-06 such sources sat under NOT-READ and the debt could not
# reach zero by any amount of reading.


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=20,
                    help="how many owed pairs to list per parameter (default 20)")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not DB_PATH.exists():
        print(f"scan_debt: no database at {DB_PATH}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB_PATH}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='v_scan_ledger'"
                            ).fetchone():
            print("scan_debt: v_scan_ledger is absent (pre-103 schema)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        status = dict(conn.execute("SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM v_scan_ledger "
                                   "GROUP BY status").fetchall())
        per_param = conn.execute(
            "SELECT l.parameter_id, t.canonical_en, "
            "SUM(l.status = 'NOT-READ'), SUM(l.status = 'READ-PARTIAL') "
            "FROM v_scan_ledger l JOIN base_parameters p USING (parameter_id) "
            "JOIN terms t ON t.term_id = p.term_id "
            "GROUP BY l.parameter_id ORDER BY l.parameter_id").fetchall()
        owed = conn.execute(
            "SELECT parameter_id, ref_id, status FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE status IN (?, ?) "
            "ORDER BY parameter_id, ref_id", DEBT).fetchall()
    finally:
        conn.close()

    total = sum(status.values())
    debt = sum(status.get(s, 0) for s in DEBT)
    print("scan_debt — (source x active parameter) pairs not yet read in full")

scripts/audit/skill_vocabulary_audit.py — every value a skill names must have a home.

WHY THIS EXISTS (CLAUDE.md rule 8; owner 2026-11-06: "ensure all terminologies and
vocabularies are correct"). A skill is a prose caller: it tells an operator which words to
type into a writer. Two walk-throughs of skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md (2026-11-06) found the
conflict mapper naming a column that no table has (`mode_s_trigger`) and population codes
the identity lens does not hold (`VIS`, `DBL`, `OFS`), and the connection skill naming
verdicts (`SUBSUMES`, `CONFLATED_VARIABLE`) with no typed home. An operator who follows
such a sentence writes prose into a free-text cell, or is refused by a writer the skill
said would accept the value -- either way the page downstream cannot join what was typed.

WHAT IT CHECKS. Every BACKTICKED token in a skill, command or agent file that is SHAPED like a
vocabulary value or an identifier (contains `_` or `-`, or is all capitals) must resolve to one
of the homes the repository holds, and to nothing else: a table, view, column, `table.column` or
CHECK vocabulary value (dbcore.check_values over every column) or a view's CASE literal; a
`db.py` verb (from `--help`) or flag (from the parser source); a registered check id; a
pipeline-contract stage or criterion id; an R-rule label (governance/research-contract.yaml); a
skill, command or agent stem; a tracked path or basename; an identity, ICF, access-need, slug,
term or gap id live in its registry; `sqlite_master` / `sqlite_sequence`; a placeholder (a token

backticked token is a value the skill tells the operator to type.

they are conventions the 2026-11-06 ruling on joined cells queues for typed columns, not
vocabulary.

retired container or a column that does not exist writes the fact into a note cell, which no
